fullAnalysis: Pinpoint #684 revolves around the word "roses." Four clues point to rose varieties or rose-related phrases: English rose, dog rose, Damask rose, and hybrid tea rose. The final clue, "Stop and smell the roses," confirms the flower theme and makes the shared connector obvious.

What makes this puzzle feel tricky at first is that the first four clues do not immediately look related. The idiom clue changes the frame from general vocabulary to flowers, and once that shift happens, each earlier clue clicks neatly into place as a rose name or rose phrase.
solutionNarrative: When I first looked at English, Dog, Damask, and (Hybrid) Tea, they did not seem to belong in the same category. The breakthrough was the clue "Stop and smell the roses," which shifted my thinking toward flowers instead of abstract wordplay. After that, the pattern became straightforward: English rose, dog rose, Damask rose, and hybrid tea rose all work cleanly, so the answer is "Words that come before “roses”."

lessons.title: Let the strongest clue reframe the puzzle
lessons.body: When a set feels disconnected, one clue often changes the whole frame of reference. Here, the idiom clue points directly to flowers.

lessons.title: Check for real phrases, not just loose associations
lessons.body: The best Pinpoint solutions usually form familiar phrases or named categories, such as dog rose or hybrid tea rose.

lessons.title: Verify every clue against one connector
lessons.body: A good answer does not solve only three or four clues. It should account for all five without forcing the wording.
